mainTopic: מוקצה and נעבד animals: their source, when the status ends, and why they are permitted to eat; טרפה on the מזבח; and the definition of אתנן
overview: This amud begins at the end of a list of normally forbidden things that were used in גדעון's sacrifice, among them מוקצה (an animal set aside for עבודה זרה) and נעבד (an animal that was itself worshipped). רבי יאשיה learns the rule of מוקצה from "תשמרו להקריב לי": an animal kept "for Me," and not for another master. Several opinions then explain how long an animal stays מוקצה. It is forbidden only until it is used for work, or handed to the idol's priests and fed their vetch, or sheared and worked. רב פפא then proves from "ממשקה ישראל" that מוקצה and נעבד animals are permitted to eat, since otherwise no פסוק would be needed to keep them off the מזבח. The גמרא challenges this from טרפה. It answers that each טרפה פסוק covers a different case: an animal that became a טרפה after it was made holy, and one that became a טרפה after it was born. A new משנה then defines אתנן, payment to a זונה, including a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים. The גמרא explains why even a hundred lambs are forbidden, and then discusses a ברייתא about payment given at a different time from the act. רבי אלעזר's answer about why an early payment does not become אתנן backward in time continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the list: service vessels, אשירה vessels and wood, set-aside and worshipped animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a list of normally forbidden things that were allowed for גדעון's sacrifice: no כלי שרת, כלי אשירה, עצי אשירה, מוקצה, and נעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And service vessels, and אשירה vessels, and אשירה wood, and a set-aside animal, and a worshipped animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list that started on the previous page. Each item is something normally forbidden in a קרבן that was allowed for גדעון's sacrifice that one night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every item here is normally a problem for a קרבן. Offering without כלי שרת is not allowed, and wood or vessels from an אשירה are forbidden. An animal set aside for idols (מוקצה) or worshipped as an idol (נעבד) cannot be brought on the מזבח. Mentioning מוקצה sets up the next question: where does the Torah teach that מוקצה is forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: A sacred vessel used for the service in the מקדש
A tree that people worship as an idol
Here: an animal set aside to be offered to an idol
An animal that was itself worshipped as an idol

phrases.english: And service vessels,
and vessels of an asheira, and wood of an asheira,
and a set-aside animal, and a worshipped animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְלִי שָׁרֵת, וּכְלִי אֲשֵׁירָה, וַעֲצֵי אֲשֵׁירָה, וּמוּקְצֶה, וְנֶעֱבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list begun on the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These items, normally forbidden for a קרבן, were permitted as a one-time exception for גדעון's sacrifice.

steps.title: The Torah source for the set-aside animal
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי בר מתנה quotes רבי יאשיה: מוקצה is learned from "תשמרו להקריב לי במועדו", meaning anything that is kept and guarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי בר מתנה said in the name of רבי יאשיה: Where does the Torah teach the law of a set-aside animal? The verse says "You shall guard to offer to Me in its time," which means anything that is guarded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a Torah source for the rule that a מוקצה animal is disqualified. It quotes the פסוק about guarding the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the word תשמרו, "you shall guard." At first the explanation sounds like it is about the guarding itself: a proper קרבן is something you keep and look after. That vague first reading is exactly what the next step attacks.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? A request for a source
From the Torah itself, not a rabbinic rule
Guarding, keeping watch over something

phrases.english: Rav Tovi bar Mattana said,
Rabbi Yoshiya said:
From where do we know the law of a set-aside animal from the Torah?
As it is said: "You shall guard to offer to Me in its time" —
anything that people guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the item מוקצה from the list and looks for its Torah source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition of מוקצה comes from the Torah, from the פסוק "תשמרו להקריב לי במועדו".

steps.title: אביי: a neglected weak lamb would then be disqualified
steps.stepSummary: אביי attacks the reading "anything that is guarded": if someone brings a weak lamb that nobody looked after, would it be unfit?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged this: If so, if someone brought a weak, starved lamb and did not look after it, would you also say it is unfit to be offered?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the explanation from the last step. He shows that, read simply, it leads to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תשמרו means a קרבן must be well guarded, then a thin, neglected lamb should be disqualified. But nobody says an animal is unfit just because its owner did not care for it well. So the plain "guarding" reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, a formal objection
"But if so...": introduces an unacceptable result
Literally "a lamb of fasting": a weak, starved lamb
"Would you also say so?": pointing to an absurd result

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying מוקצה is permitted. He only rejects one way of reading the פסוק. The prohibition itself stays.

phrases.english: Abaye challenged it:
But if so,
if he brought a weak, starved lamb,
phrases.notes: Some versions say "you brought" (round brackets); the corrected wording in square brackets says "he brought."

phrases.english: and did not look after it,
would you also say it is not fit to be offered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the interpretation of תשמרו given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of תשמרו as "anything that is guarded"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: by that reading, an unguarded weak lamb would be disqualified, which nobody holds.

steps.title: The key word is "to Me": not to another master, meaning idolatry
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the stress is on the word לי, "to Me", and not to another master. The only other "master" people offer to is עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I meant the verse "You shall guard to offer to Me in its time" this way: "to Me," and not to another master. And who is the other that people offer to? You must say it is idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer explains that the proof comes from the word "to Me," not from the guarding itself. So a neglected lamb is fine. Only an animal kept for an idol is ruled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not about how well the animal was cared for. It is about whom it was kept for. An animal kept "for another master," meaning עבודה זרה, cannot be offered to ה׳. That is exactly מוקצה, so אביי's weak lamb is no longer a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: I am saying, I meant
Another master: any power other than ה׳
"You must say": the only possible answer
Idol worship

steps.whatToRemember: The source for מוקצה is the word לי in "תשמרו להקריב לי": an animal kept for an idol may not be offered to ה׳. Care or neglect of the animal makes no difference.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I was speaking about "You shall guard to offer to Me in its time" —
"to Me," and not to another master,
And who is the other that people offer to?
You must say: this is idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא ״תִּשְׁמְרוּ לְהַקְרִיב לִי בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ״ קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי by clarifying which word in the פסוק carries the proof
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the intended reading: the derivation rests on לי, not on שימור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The derivation was about guarding the animal, so an unguarded weak lamb would be unfit
steps.terutzMaskana: The derivation is "to Me and not to another master", so only an animal kept for עבודה זרה is excluded

steps.title: רב יצחק: set-aside status lasts until it is used for work
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק (quoted by רבא בר רב אדא) says a מוקצה animal is forbidden only until the idol's attendants use it for work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב אדא said in the name of רב יצחק: A set-aside animal is forbidden only until they do work with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks how long an animal stays מוקצה. רב יצחק gives the first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the idol's attendants use the animal for work, it is clear they no longer plan to offer it to the idol. So it loses its "set aside for an idol" status and is no longer forbidden for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden
Until they do work with it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse מוקצה here with the שבת idea of מוקצה. Here it means an animal set aside for idol worship.

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Adda said,
Rav Yitzchak said:
A set-aside animal is not forbidden
except until they do work with it.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, "with it," is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוּקְצֶה אָסוּר אֶלָּא עַד שֶׁיַּעַבְדוּ בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the source for מוקצה, defines when the status ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal set aside for idolatry stays forbidden until it is used for work.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: until it is handed over to the idol's priests
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן: the animal is forbidden only until it is handed over to the priests of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Until they hand it over to the priests of idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion gives a different point where מוקצה status ends: when the animal is handed over to the idol's priests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, no work is needed. Once the animal is given to the idol's priests, it ends its "set aside" stage and loses its מוקצה status. This is an earlier and easier stopping point than רב יצחק's.

keyTerms.meaning: That they hand it over
Priests or attendants of an idol

steps.whatToRemember: Two views on when מוקצה ends: רב יצחק says when it is used for work, and רבי יוחנן says when it is handed to the idol's priests.

phrases.english: Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Until they hand it over
to the priests of idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עַד שֶׁיִּמְסְרוּהוּ לְכוּמְרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing definition of when מוקצה status ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal set aside for idolatry stays forbidden until it is handed to the idol's priests.

steps.title: בהא's version: forbidden only until it is fed the idol's vetch
steps.stepSummary: בהא quotes רבי יוחנן: a מוקצה animal stays forbidden only until it is fed vetch belonging to עבודה זרה. After that it loses its מוקצה status.
steps.simpleTranslation: בהא says in the name of רבי יוחנן: the set-aside animal is forbidden only until they feed it the idol's vetch.
steps.whatsHappening: A third version of רבי יוחנן's rule is given, this time by בהא. The animal stays forbidden only until it is fed the idol's animal food. After that it is no longer מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, עולא quoted רבי יוחנן as saying the animal stays forbidden until it is handed to the priests of עבודה זרה. בהא's version names a different ending point: when the animal eats the idol's own food. This sets up the question of whether the two quotes disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Vetch, a cheap bean-like plant used as animal feed

phrases.english: Baha says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
Until they feed it vetch of idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רבי יוחנן's rule alongside עולא's version in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה animal stays forbidden only until it has been fed the idol's vetch. After that it is no longer מוקצה.

steps.title: Does Baha disagree with עולא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks בהא whether his version disagrees with עולא's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to בהא: Are you arguing with עולא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא notices that בהא and עולא quote רבי יוחנן differently and asks if they truly disagree. This sets up בהא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said the moment is when the animal is handed over to the priests. בהא said it is when the animal is fed the idol's vetch. רבי אבא wants to know whether these are two different rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you disagree / argue

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Baha:
Do you disagree with Ulla?
phrases.notes: עולא's version is the one from step 6: until it is handed to the idol's priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how בהא's version fits with עולא's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בהא's and עולא's quotes of רבי יוחנן are two opposing rules.

steps.title: No argument: עולא meant the same case
steps.stepSummary: בהא answers that there is no disagreement. עולא was also speaking about a case where the animal was fed the idol's vetch.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. When עולא said it, he too meant a case where they fed it the idol's vetch.
steps.whatsHappening: בהא shows that the two quotes are really one rule. עולא's case of handing over to the priests is a case where the animal also eats the idol's food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being handed to the priests by itself is not the key. What counts is that once the priests have it, they feed it the idol's vetch. So both versions point to the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Fed / gave to eat (Aramaic)

steps.whatToRemember: According to בהא, both quotes of רבי יוחנן agree: the animal stays forbidden as מוקצה only until it has eaten the idol's food.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
Ulla too, when he said it,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּשָׁפֵי לֵיהּ כַּרְשִׁינֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: it was where they fed it vetch of idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, עוּלָּא נָמֵי כִּי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's question by reconciling the two versions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולא's 'handed to the priests' refers to a case where they also fed it the idol's vetch, so there is no disagreement.

steps.title: רבי אבא credits ארץ ישראל for בהא's wisdom
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא praises בהא's skill in reconciling the teachings and says he gained it from going up to ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: בהא knows how to explain teachings, but had he not gone up there, he would not have known. ארץ ישראל caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא comments on the previous answer. He says בהא's ability to settle the contradiction came from his time in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side comment about the person, not a new law. It reflects the idea that living and learning in ארץ ישראל sharpens a person's understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: To answer / reconcile a difficulty
A teaching or halachic statement
Went up (moved to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Baha knows how to explain the teaching,
but had he not gone up there,
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל. בהא came up from בבל.

phrases.english: he would not have known,
for Eretz Yisrael caused it for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: יָדַע בְּהָא לְשַׁנּוֹיֵי שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side remark about the sage who gave the answer in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בהא's skill at reconciling teachings came from going up to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רב יצחק: בהא learned in both places
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק pushes back: בהא's wisdom came from both בבל and ארץ ישראל, not from ארץ ישראל alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק said to him: בהא was from here and from there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק disagrees with רבי אבא's comment. He says בהא's wisdom came from learning in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא gave all the credit to ארץ ישראל. רב יצחק answers that בהא had already learned in בבל, so both places formed him.

keyTerms.meaning: From here and from there (both places)

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak said to him:
Baha was from here and from there.
phrases.notes: He means בהא learned Torah both in בבל and in ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אבא's claim that ארץ ישראל alone made בהא wise.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the claim about where בהא's wisdom came from. The halacha is not affected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אבא ignored that בהא had also learned in בבל.

steps.title: רב חנניא טריטאה: forbidden only until it is sheared and worked
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניא טריטאה taught before רבי יוחנן that a מוקצה animal is forbidden only until an 'act' is done with it, and he explained this as being sheared and used for work.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חנניא טריטאה taught before רבי יוחנן: a set-aside animal is forbidden only until they do an act with it. He taught it and he also explained it: What is 'an act'? Until it is sheared and they work with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching about when a מוקצה animal stops being forbidden. The teacher explains his own vague word 'act' as shearing the animal and working with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רב יצחק's view in step 5, that the animal stays forbidden only until the idol's servants use it for work. The general word 'act' is defined in concrete terms: once it is sheared and worked, it is clear it will not be offered to the idol, so it is no longer מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: An act or deed done with the animal
That it be sheared
And they work with it

steps.whatToRemember: An animal set aside for עבודה זרה is forbidden for the מזבח, but only until something is done with it that shows it will not be offered to the idol: being used for work, handed to the priests and fed the idol's food, or sheared and worked.

phrases.english: As Rav Chananya Terita taught
before Rabbi Yochanan:
A set-aside animal is not forbidden
except until they do an act with it,
He taught it, and he himself explained it:
phrases.notes: Some versions say "and then" (round brackets); the corrected wording in square brackets says "and he himself."

phrases.english: What is "an act"?
Until it is sheared and they work with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי רַב חֲנַנְיָא טְרִיטָאָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side story to the main question of when a מוקצה animal stops being forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוקצה animal stays forbidden only until it has been sheared and used for work.

steps.title: The worshipped animal: what is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's case of a נעבד animal, one that was itself worshipped, and asks where the law comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Which is a worshipped animal, etc." From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, the animal that was itself worshipped. It asks for the source in the Torah, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was מוקצה, an animal set aside to be offered to an idol. Now the topic changes to נעבד, an animal that was itself treated as a god. The משנה rules that both of these animals are permitted to eat, and the question asks for the source of that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that was itself worshipped as an idol
From where are these matters derived? (asking for a source)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מוקצה and נעבד. מוקצה is set aside to be offered to an idol. נעבד is itself worshipped as the idol.

phrases.english: "Which is the worshipped animal, etc."
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ נֶעֱבָד כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of מוקצה to the next case in the משנה, נעבד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the משנה's ruling that the מוקצה and נעבד animals are permitted to an ordinary person.

steps.title: The source from ״ממשקה ישראל״ shows these animals are permitted to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the source is ״ממשקה ישראל״: offerings come only from what is permitted to ישראל. Since a פסוק was needed to exclude these animals from the מזבח, they must be permitted to an ordinary person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The פסוק says "from the well-watered pastures of ישראל," meaning from what is permitted to ישראל. If you thought these animals were forbidden to an ordinary person, why would a פסוק be needed to exclude them from the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from Step 13. From the פסוק that keeps נעבד and מוקצה animals off the מזבח, he proves that they are permitted to an ordinary person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches that offerings must come from what ישראל may use. רב פפא adds a second point. If these animals were already forbidden to eat, it would be obvious they cannot go on the מזבח. The fact that a פסוק was needed shows they are permitted to an ordinary person.

keyTerms.meaning: "From the well-watered pastures of ישראל": offerings must come from what is permitted to ישראל
An ordinary person (using it for himself, such as eating it)
"The Most High": use for הקדש or for the מזבח
"It would enter your mind": if you were to think
To exclude them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a rule of logic that the next step will test: something forbidden to an ordinary person should not need a פסוק to keep it off the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For the verse says: "From the well-watered pastures of Israel,"
meaning from what is permitted to Israel.
And if you were to think they are forbidden to an ordinary person,
phrases.notes: "They" means the מוקצה and נעבד animals.

phrases.english: why would I need a verse
to exclude them from the Most High?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב פפא דאמר קרא ממשקה ישראל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question asked in Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ״ממשקה ישראל״: offerings must come from what is permitted to ישראל. Because a פסוק was needed, these animals must be permitted to an ordinary person.

steps.title: But a טרפה is forbidden to eat and still needs a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's logic. A טרפה is forbidden to an ordinary person, yet a פסוק still excludes it from the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that wherever something is forbidden to an ordinary person, no פסוק is needed? But a טרפה is forbidden to an ordinary person, and a פסוק still excludes it from the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reasoning of Step 14 by pointing to the case of a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumed that a פסוק excluding something from the מזבח proves it is permitted to eat. The טרפה seems to disprove this. It is forbidden to eat, and the Torah still bothers to exclude it from the מזבח. So the existence of a פסוק may not prove anything about eating.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect; it is forbidden to eat
No פסוק is needed
The פסוק excludes it

phrases.english: And wherever things are forbidden to an ordinary person,
is no verse needed?
But a tereifa, which is forbidden to an ordinary person,
and a verse excludes it from the Most High!

steps.triggerLanguage: וכל היכא דאסירי להדיוט לא בעי קרא והא טרפה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic that Step 14 used
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that a פסוק would not be needed for something already forbidden to an ordinary person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה is forbidden to eat, yet the Torah still gives a פסוק excluding it from the מזבח. So a פסוק can be needed even for something forbidden to eat.

steps.title: The ברייתא that excludes a טרפה from the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא. The extra words ״מן הבקר״ in the second פסוק come to exclude a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: when the Torah says "of the herd" further down, it did not need to say it. It is there to exclude a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for its challenge from Step 15, showing that a פסוק really does exclude a טרפה from the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already said "from the herd" in the earlier פסוק. Repeating it in the next פסוק is extra. The ברייתא uses that extra wording to exclude a טרפה, which confirms the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: "Below": in the following פסוק
"There is no need to say it": the words are extra
To exclude

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
When it says "of the herd" below,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3. The earlier פסוק, ויקרא 1:2, already said "from the herd."

phrases.english: there was no need for the verse to say it,
rather, it comes to exclude the tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא כשהוא אומר מן הבקר למטה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in Step 15
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that a פסוק excludes a טרפה from the מזבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the extra words ״מן הבקר״ in ויקרא 1:3

steps.title: The פסוק was needed for an animal that became a טרפה after it was made holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק for טרפה was needed for one case. If the animal became a טרפה after it was made holy, we might have thought it is still allowed on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought the rule applies only when the animal became a טרפה and then was made holy. But if it was made holy first and only later became a טרפה, I would say it is permitted for the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Steps 15-16 by explaining why the טרפה case still needed its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was already a טרפה before it was made holy is obviously unfit, just as רב פפא's logic says. The hard case is an animal that was made holy while healthy and only became a טרפה later. We might have thought its holiness keeps it fit for the מזבח, so a פסוק was needed. That means רב פפא's logic still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was needed": the פסוק has a real purpose
"These words apply": the rule is limited to this case
It became a טרפה
It was made holy (consecrated)
I would say

steps.whatToRemember: A פסוק is not needed to forbid on the מזבח what is already forbidden to eat. The טרפה פסוק is needed only for an animal that became a טרפה after it was made holy. So רב פפא's proof stands: מוקצה and נעבד animals are permitted to an ordinary person.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not mean that a טרפה is usually allowed on the מזבח. It deals only with the special case where the animal was made holy first and became a טרפה afterward.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
since you might have thought to say:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי — דְּנִטְרְפָה וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְקַדְּשָׁה,
phrases.english: This applies only where it became a tereifa and afterward was consecrated,
but if it was consecrated and afterward became a tereifa,
I would say it should be permitted to the Most High.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 15-16 and keeps Step 14 standing
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to a case that is not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal that became a טרפה after it was made holy might still be fit for the מזבח because of its holiness
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that even such an animal is excluded. Something forbidden to eat from the start needs no פסוק, so רב פפא's proof holds.

steps.title: Another verse already excludes a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 17. The rule that a טרפה cannot be offered already seems to come from the מעשר בהמה verse, ״כל אשר יעבור תחת השבט״.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we already learn this from here: 'Whatever passes under the rod' excludes a טרפה, which cannot pass under it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. It points to a different פסוק that already seems to teach that a טרפה cannot be brought on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the גמרא said ״מן הבקר״ was needed for an animal that became a טרפה after it was made holy. Now it asks why we need that, since ״יעבור תחת השבט״ already excludes a טרפה. An animal with a badly broken leg cannot walk under the counting rod, so it is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The rod used when counting animals for מעשר בהמה; every tenth animal is marked as holy
Excluding; this word or phrase leaves something out
But isn't it derived from here? A way of saying the law already has a source

phrases.english: But isn't it derived from here:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the rule that a טרפה cannot be brought on the מזבח.

phrases.english: "Whatever passes under the rod,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:32, the פסוק about מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: excluding a טרפה, which cannot pass under it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 17 by pointing to a second source for the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״מן הבקר״ is needed to exclude a טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״יעבור תחת השבט״ already excludes a טרפה, then ״מן הבקר״ seems to repeat it for nothing.

steps.title: Both verses are needed for different kinds of טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The ״יעבור״ פסוק is also needed. Without it we would think that only an animal born a טרפה is forbidden, and that one which was healthy at first and later became a טרפה is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse was also needed. You might have thought the rule applies only where the animal was never fit, meaning it was born a טרפה. But where it was fit, came out into the world, and only later became a טרפה, you might say it is allowed on the מזבח. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Each פסוק teaches a different case, so neither one is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that only an animal that was never healthy (born a טרפה) is kept off the מזבח. ״יעבור״ teaches that even an animal born healthy that later became a טרפה is forbidden. ״מן הבקר״ (step 17) is still needed for the case where it became a טרפה after it was made holy.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say; introduces a mistaken first thought
A time of fitness; a period when the animal was healthy and could have been offered
It teaches us; the פסוק comes to rule out the mistaken thought

steps.whatToRemember: There are three stages of טרפה: born a טרפה, became a טרפה after birth, and became a טרפה after being made holy. One born a טרפה is plainly excluded. Each of the two later cases needs its own פסוק, because there we might have thought it is permitted to the מזבח. So the טרפה verses do not undercut רב פפא.

phrases.english: That one was also needed,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the ״יעבור תחת השבט״ פסוק.

phrases.english: for it would enter your mind to say:
These words apply only where
it never had a time of fitness,
meaning it was born a טרפה from its mother's womb;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּהָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר,
phrases.english: but where it did have a time of fitness,
and it came out into the air of the world,
and only afterward became a טרפה —
I would say it should be permitted to the Most High,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by giving each פסוק its own case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source is needed for a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an animal that was never fit (born a טרפה) is forbidden. One that was fit and later became a טרפה would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״יעבור״ forbids even an animal that became a טרפה after birth, and ״מן הבקר״ forbids one that became a טרפה after it was made holy.

steps.title: The משנה defines אתנן
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה explains what counts as אתנן. A lamb given to a זונה as payment is forbidden, even if there are a hundred lambs. If someone pays so that his slave can be with another person's maidservant, רבי מאיר says it is not אתנן and חכמים say it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is אתנן? Someone says to a prostitute, 'Here is this lamb as your fee.' Even if there are a hundred, all are forbidden. Likewise, someone says to his friend, 'Here is this lamb, and let your maidservant lie with my slave.' רבי מאיר says it is not אתנן, and the חכמים say it is אתנן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains what an אתנן is, one of the animals that cannot be brought as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic case is payment to a זונה, and the number of animals does not matter. The disputed case is payment given to the owner of the maidservant, not to the woman herself, and for a relationship that is not between two Jews. רבי מאיר does not count it as אתנן. חכמים do.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment given to a זונה; it is forbidden as a קרבן
A prostitute
A lamb
A non-Jewish maidservant
The Sages; the majority opinion

phrases.english: MISHNA: And which is an אתנן?
One who says to a prostitute:
"Here is this lamb as your fee,"
even if they are a hundred, all of them are forbidden.
And likewise one who says to his friend:
"Here is this lamb,
and let your maidservant lie with my slave" —
רבי מאיר says: it is not an אתנן;
and the Rabbis say: it is an אתנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, after the discussion of נעבד and טרפה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Payment to a זונה is אתנן no matter how many animals are given. Payment for a maidservant to be with a slave is a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים.

steps.title: What case does 'a hundred' describe?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'even if they are a hundred, all are forbidden' and asks what situation it is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Even if they are a hundred, all are forbidden. What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by quoting one line. It asks what case that line means, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'even a hundred' suggest the משנה is teaching something surprising. The גמרא wants to find the case where that would really be a new point.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? A request to pin down the exact situation

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Master said:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is the משנה we just learned.

phrases.english: And even if they are a hundred, all of them are forbidden.
What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case the משנה means by 'even a hundred lambs are all forbidden'

steps.title: If she was paid a hundred animals, that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the simple reading, that she was paid a hundred animals, and rejects it. That would be obvious, since one animal or a hundred makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she took a hundred animals as her pay, it is obvious that all are forbidden. What difference does it make to me whether it is one or a hundred!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simplest explanation of the משנה and shows that it can't be right, because the משנה would be teaching nothing new. This sets up a search for a better explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all hundred animals were her payment, each one is payment, so of course all are forbidden. The משנה would not need 'even' for that. So the case must be something less obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
It is obvious; so why would the משנה need to say it?

keyTerms.term: מָה לִי חַד, מָה לִי מְאָה
keyTerms.meaning: What difference is one or a hundred? The number does not change the law

phrases.english: If we say that she took a hundred animals as her pay —
it is obvious that all of them are forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי חַד, מָה לִי מְאָה!
phrases.english: what difference is it to me whether one or a hundred!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 21's question and rejects it at once.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The simple reading that the hundred animals were all her stated payment
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the משנה's 'even a hundred' teach nothing new, since the number of animals does not matter.

steps.title: She agreed to one lamb but he gave a hundred
steps.stepSummary: The 'hundred' case is where she agreed to one lamb as her fee and he gave her a hundred. All of them are forbidden, because they all come from the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where she took one lamb as her fee, and he gave her a hundred. All of them come from the force of the אתנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real meaning of 'even a hundred.' The fee she agreed to was only one lamb, but he gave her a hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 threw out the simple reading, since a hundred lambs paid as the fee is obvious. The new point is about the extra 99. You might think they are just a gift and allowed. The משנה teaches they are forbidden too, because they were all given as part of the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for... (introduces the real case being discussed)
A fee or wage
From the force of, coming because of

steps.whatToRemember: Anything given as part of the payment to a זונה is אתנן, even more than the price she agreed to.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where she takes one as her fee
and he gave her one hundred
for they all come from the force of the payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 22 rejected the simple reading, this gives the real case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the משנה means by 'even a hundred are forbidden.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fee agreed on was one lamb, but he gave a hundred. All are forbidden as אתנן.

steps.title: Payment without the act, or the act without payment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if he gave her something but did not have relations with her, or had relations but did not give, 'her payment' is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If he gave to her and did not come to her, or came to her and did not give to her, her payment is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about when a payment to a זונה becomes אתנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to teach that both the giving and the act must be present for אתנן. The גמרא will question its exact wording right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
He had relations with her
Permitted

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he gave to her but did not have relations with her,
or had relations with her but did not give to her,
her payment is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נָתַן לָהּ וְלֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the definition of אתנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without both the giving and the act, her payment is permitted.

steps.title: The wording of the ברייתא does not make sense
steps.stepSummary: If there was no act, why call it 'her payment'? And if he never gave her anything, what is permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: He gave to her and did not come to her, you call that 'her payment'? And further, he came to her and did not give to her, what did he give her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's wording. Both cases, read literally, do not fit the words 'her payment is permitted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case nothing was paid for, so it is not 'her payment' at all. In the second case nothing was given, so there is no object that could be permitted. The literal reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: You call it
And furthermore

phrases.english: He gave to her and did not have relations with her,
do you call it 'her payment'?

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ, בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְלֹא נָתַן לָהּ,
phrases.english: And furthermore, he had relations with her and did not give to her,
what did he give her?

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן לָהּ וְלֹא בָּא עָלֶיהָ, ״אֶתְנַנָּה״ קָרֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two cases in the ברייתא of step 24.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without an act it is not 'payment,' and without giving there is nothing to permit. So the literal wording fails.

steps.title: Payment given before or after the act, at a different time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means he paid first and had relations later, or had relations first and paid later. In both cases the payment is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it teaches: He gave to her and afterward came to her, or came to her and afterward gave to her, her payment is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. It is about payment and act that both happened, but not at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both cases have a real payment and a real act, so 'her payment' fits. The new point is that timing matters. When the giving is separated from the act, the payment does not become אתנן.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches (a rereading of the text)
And afterward

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is no longer about missing payment or a missing act. Both happened, but at separate times.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן לָהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא עָלֶיהָ;
phrases.english: he gave to her, and afterward had relations with her;

phrases.aramaic: בָּא עָלֶיהָ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָתַן לָהּ —
phrases.english: he had relations with her, and afterward gave to her —
her payment is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא spoke of payment with no act, or an act with no payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: It speaks of payment given before or after the act, with time between them. Such a payment is permitted.

steps.title: Why doesn't an early payment become אתנן backward in time?
steps.stepSummary: If he paid first and the act came later, the payment should become אתנן backward once the act happens. רבי אלעזר is about to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the status of אתנן take effect on it retroactively! רבי אלעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first case of step 26. Once the act happens, why doesn't the earlier gift become אתנן looking back? The line ends by starting רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamb was given for the act, so after the act it should count as payment from the start. That would make it forbidden and go against the ברייתא. רבי אלעזר's answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it take effect
Retroactively, backward in time

phrases.english: But let the status of payment take effect on it retroactively?
phrases.notes: This is about the first case, where he paid before the act.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first case of the rereading in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that payment given before the act is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the act happens, the earlier gift should count as payment backward in time and become forbidden.
